findings.reason: The authentic three-tile original contains a deterministic period-two example and its full computation but no illustration. A concrete two-vertex directed graph together with a time-indexed law strip materially clarifies the contrast between alternation of the one-time laws and convergence after averaging. This is a warranted explanatory diagram addition under the expanded scope, not a defect in the existing proof.
findings.action: Added a final Remarks section with the transition graph, n=0,1,2,3 point-mass strip, and separately identified Cesaro average limit.

correction: Appended explanatory Remarks and one native TikZ illustration; all original source bytes, including the complete mathematical example, verification, dependencies and publication status, are preserved as a prefix.

source_lines_after.description: New Remarks, explanatory conventions and TikZ illustration

diagram_math_checks.objects: State space E={0,1}; transition matrix p acts on probability row laws on E.
diagram_math_checks.check: The upper graph has exactly two state vertices and exactly two directed edges, 0 to 1 and 1 to 0, both weighted 1. There are no self-loops, matching p(0,0)=p(1,1)=0. Each vertex has indegree one and outdegree one. The two edges were explicitly drawn and both arrowheads are visible.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Existing Given and verification step 1.1; local transition-matrix definition identifies p(x,y) with the one-step singleton probability.

diagram_math_checks.check: The strip is delta_0 at n=0, delta_1 at n=1, delta_0 at n=2 and delta_1 at n=3. Each p arrow applies the same transition matrix to a row law; delta_0 p=delta_1 and delta_1 p=delta_0. The final arrow continues alternation rather than asserting a limit.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification step 1.1 proves p^(2m)=I and p^(2m+1)=p including m=0, and step 2.3 proves nonconvergence. The local zero-step convention is p^(0)=I.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Period and averaged probability law overline(mu)_n.
diagram_math_checks.check: The period label 2 follows from positive returns at precisely 2,4,6,...; n=0 is not counted as a positive return. The displayed average sums k=0 through n-1, divided by n, and tends to pi=(1/2,1/2); even n has equally many of the two point masses, while odd n has one extra delta_0.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification steps 3.2, 4.1 and boundary step 5.1, with local period definition excluding zero. The figure does not assert aperiodicity or ordinary convergence.
